text:
sam: Heads-up — p99 for /v1/generate jumped from ~220ms to ~1.2s during the 14:00 load sweep. p50/p95 fine. Traces point to kernel swap + KV detach on a subset of requests. Anyone seen this pattern before?

alex: Can you paste one of the offending traces/serving logs?

sam: Posting sanitized snippet from the trace (req id truncated):
```
[14:01:02.412] req=abc123 seq_len=3860 kernel=opt_kernel_v2 -> fallback_safe_v1 kernel_switch_ms=175 kv_hit=false batch_wait_ms=12 gen_ms=820 total_ms=1199
[14:01:02.413] reason: seq_len>2048 -> selected fallback_safe_v1 (fallback path has no fused-attn kernels)
```

maria: Oh — long prompt + high model depth will trigger the fallback kernel. opt_kernel_v2 only handles <=2048 in our runtime right now. That kernel_switch is expensive because we reconfigure memory layout + disable fused kernels.

devon: Also noticed many of those requests include synchronous tool calls (embed/lookup) in the middle of generation. Tool-call loops cause generator to pause, which flushes KV to disk in some in-process configs and forces full KV rehydration when generation resumes. That KV rehydrate is ~180-220ms.

sam: Repro steps I used in the sim harness:
```bash
# repro: long prompt + toolchain that does 2 sync tool calls mid-gen
./tools/sim_client --url http://localhost:8080/v1/generate \
  --prompt-file long_prompt.txt --toolchain sync_lookup --concurrency 12 --seed 42
```
repro result: p50=240ms, p95=460ms, p99=1.15s (matches prod spike)

infra-bot: Autoscale and infra logs show no GPU contention or host OOMs during the window. CPUs and GPU metrics stable. The correlation coefficient between kernel_switch events and p99 is 0.72 for the 14:00 window.

alex: I profiled microbatching behavior: batch_target=16, batch_max_wait_ms=20, adaptive=false for this route. With skewed length distribution (1 long request + 15 short), the long request causes the fused-kernel selection to flip for the whole batch in some code paths, or we end up with head-of-line blocking where a large sequence holds the device for much longer.

maria: For clarity: two separate mechanisms are amplifying latency — (A) kernel fallback/selection overhead for long sequences, (B) KV cache thrash / rehydrate due to synchronous tool calls that break the streaming path. They multiply when both occur on the same request.

devon: Quick numbers from micro-profiling: additional cost breakdown on offending requests: kernel_switch+reconfig ~140-200ms, KV rehydrate ~180-220ms, batching head-of-line/blocking adds variable 50-300ms depending on concurrency. Totals line up with ~1.1-1.3s p99.

sam: Proposed immediate mitigations (fast, low-risk):
- add a low-latency route header (x-pref: low_latency) that bypasses microbatching for latency-sensitive clients
- reduce batch_max_wait_ms to 5ms for the route owning interactive traffic
- enable KV eager-pin for generator processes that do sync tool calls (preload instead of rehydrate)

alex: Medium-term: increase opt_kernel supported seq_len (e.g., extend fused kernels to 4096) or implement chunked attention path that stays in the optimized kernel. Also add length-aware batching so we don't mix >2k tokens with short requests.

maria: Long-term: detect tool-call patterns and convert sync tool calls to an async pattern that streams placeholders and then patches results back without tearing the KV context. Also implement per-request kernel warm-start so repeated long-seq requests reuse kernel state without full reconfig.

devon: Quick config snippet to try in staging for route "/v1/generate":
```json
{"batching": {"enabled": true, "batch_target": 8, "batch_max_wait_ms": 5, "length_buckets": [0,512,2048,4096]}, "prefer_low_latency_header": true, "kv": {"eager_pin": true}}
```

ops-bot: Rolling config change staged to canary (10%): batching.max_wait_ms -> 5ms for interactive routes. Monitor p99 for 30m. :construction:

sam: After canary (10%) we saw p99 drop from ~1.2s -> ~380ms for that cohort, p95 unchanged. Good signal this is batching wait + kernel/mix problem.

alex: Remaining work items (tracked in GH):
- length-aware batching + bucketing (short/med/long)
- kernel warm-start + reduce reconfig latency
- KV eager-pin toggle and async tool handling RFC
- metric slicing: kernel_switch_count + kv_rehydrate_count per request

maria: Can we add a perf alert for kernel_switch_rate > 0.05 in a minute window for interactive routes? That will catch regressions early.

devon: PR to sim harness with toolchain repro and perf test is ready (link: https://github.com/redwood/sim/pull/412). Please review.

sam: Thanks — good triage. Next steps: ship the canary change to 50% if the 30m window stays green, then follow with the batching bucket change in a minor release. :thumbsup:

alex: +1 — I'll own the length-aware batching task.

maria: I'll draft the RFC for async tool handling and KV eager-pin details.

infra-bot: Canary window closed — no infra errors, p99 improved for canary cohort.

sam: Great, closing the immediate incident. Will follow up on action items. :eyes:
